question: The Banaras session of the Indian National Congress in 1905 was presided over by ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gopal Krishna Gokhale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Banaras session of the Indian National Congress in 1905 was presided over by **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**, a prominent leader and social reformer.
 
• Gokhale was a key advocate of **moderate politics** within the Congress, focusing on constitutional reforms and dialogue with British authorities.
 
• The Banaras session marked a pivotal moment as it addressed the **Partition of Bengal (1905)**, which created widespread unrest in India.
 
• Under Gokhale’s leadership, the Congress strongly condemned the partition and emphasized the need for **Swadeshi (self-reliance) and boycott of British goods**.
 
• Gokhale's vision during the session laid the foundation for future strategies in India's freedom movement, blending moderation with a growing emphasis on self-reliance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Partition of Bengal (1905):**

 
 
• It was carried out by Lord Curzon, the then Viceroy of India, citing administrative convenience as the reason.
 
• The partition divided Bengal into East Bengal (Muslim-majority) and West Bengal (Hindu-majority), which led to widespread protests.
 
• The move was seen as an attempt to divide and rule by creating communal divisions.
 
 
 
• **Swadeshi Movement:**
 
 
• Launched as a response to the Partition of Bengal, it urged Indians to boycott British goods and promote indigenous products.
 
• The movement also emphasized self-reliance in education, industries, and governance.
 
 
 
• **Role of Gopal Krishna Gokhale:**
 
 
• Gokhale was a disciple of social reformer Mahadev Govind Ranade and a mentor to Mahatma Gandhi.
 
• He founded the **Servants of India Society** in 1905 to promote education and social reforms.
 
 
 
• **Moderates vs. Extremists in INC:**
 
 
• The early 1900s saw a growing rift in the Congress between Moderates (like Gokhale) and Extremists (like Bal Gangadhar Tilak).
 
• Moderates advocated dialogue and reforms, while Extremists demanded direct action and self-rule.
